קורה אין זה 'כזמנם', כפי שלא ייתכן שהגרגירים והשעורה לא יהיו בשלים בשנה אחת, בשנה אחרת הם יהיו שלמים ובשנה שלישית הם יהיו [ראויים] לקציר. וכן לא ייתכן שבשנה אחת החיטה כולה תהיה רטובה בחג השבועות ובשנה אחרת תהיה ראויה לקציר. לכל מצווה שבכל חודש יש צורה שנלמדת מסימנים [שמצויים] בשדה ותמיד חלים עליה. הוא הוסיף בדברים כגון הדברים האלה, ואין צורך להזכירם. 13. והדברים שהוא ציין הם מפליאים מאוד. פלא הוא שאדם כמותו, למרות פקחותו וחוכמתו, מביא ראיה כגון זה שאין בה צורך והיא אף סותרת בהכרח את דבריו הקודמים שהבאנו בשער התשעה עשר. שהרי אנו עדים לחילוף השנים ולדברים שקורים בהן שגורמים לאיחור בהבשלת התבואה ובהיותה ראויה להיקצר לאחר שהוא נראה והוא מוכן לכך. ואילו חיפוש האביב בשבט היה חובה הרי שלא היה ניתן לשנות זאת, וקריאת המגילה היא בחודש השניים עשר כדברי המקרא שציין בעל אותה דעה (אסתר ט:לא) 'בזמניהם', הרי שאין בזה הוכחה כלל ואלו דברים ריקים.
content.english: 1. The questioner said: Is it possible that spring and the day of waving the Omer are included in the finding of the harvest, whether the festival came early or not, whether it was in that [month] or not? And he said that one of the Karaite scholars of speculation leaned [toward] this view, and in doing so he nullified the general agreement, since this contradicts the Scripture. The Torah explicitly states that this depends on the harvest, saying (Deuteronomy 16:9) "from when the sickle begins [to cut] the standing grain." And he further said: Whoever claims that there is an order here, the order only applies after the completion of the days of Passover. The one responding to this will say: We found one verse in the Torah that defines the term aviv (spring), saying (Leviticus 2:14) "fresh ears parched with fire, crushed new grain." In saying "new grain" it described this as ripe kernels and in saying "parched with fire" it described them as wet. And so it said (ibid.) "your first fruits." And nowhere else is this mentioned [and spring] is not described in any other way. 2. And he said: If someone seeks in the verse (Exodus 9:31) "for the barley was aviv" proof that this refers to a single stalk that the cold struck and uprooted, behold stalks have many forms: that which is defined, which ripens early and precedes others, is fresh ears parched with fire, crushed new grain. The new grain (carmel) is that which has full and congealed kernels, that does not drip, or that is like dough. [The main thing is] that it should be something that has a cut preserving the form of the kernel, but that is not dry, for it is not the way of new grain to be dry. And he said that this happens at the beginning of the month of Nisan or before it, for it is impossible that the proven thing should come before the proof [itself], rather it is the way of signs and proofs that they precede the things proven, or [at least] they come together. And he said: I am amazed at one who thinks that [one can] recognize [the month of] Nisan only after ten or thirteen days. And he cited the words of the Torah that we mentioned before (Exodus 40:2) "on the first day of the first month" which is mentioned before the beginning of Nisan, and said: It is impossible that the first month should enter and one day of it pass without its sign coming before it or together with it. 3. We will discuss all parts of his words. Regarding his adherence to the idea that the proof precedes the thing proven, if this were so it would not necessitate from this {846} that one must recognize the month of spring before its onset. For we said in the seventh gate of the fourth treatise that every commandment has a purpose, [and the commandment itself] is known only after its purpose is known. Since this is so, one must know what is the purpose in the obligation regarding the first month. It has already become clear that the purpose in this is nothing but Passover and the things related to it such as eating unleavened bread, celebrating the festival, waving the Omer, the seven days that come afterward and so on. For we do not find any significance to the obligation regarding the first month before the fourteenth day, and the need for proof through spring is only for the things we mentioned. And if we find [spring] on the morning of the fourteenth day and make the Passover offering in the evening of [that day] then the proof certainly preceded the thing proven, and his claim [of that man] is void. 4. And his words regarding (Exodus 40:2) "on the first day of the first month" we have already refuted in the eighteenth gate, and there we also noted their other claims and refuted them as well. We will add and say that if things were as he says and it was truly necessary for the proof to precede the thing proven, we would not be required to recognize the month of spring before its onset in order to understand the purpose of the commandment which is Passover as we noted. And likewise someone can dispute this and say that not every proof works this way, since there are proofs that come together with the thing proven and there are those that come only afterward. For example, in the eighteenth gate we noted regarding the new moon that sometimes it is seen an hour after the day begins, and its sighting [testifies] that the new month and holy convocation apply from the beginning of that day, from sunset, since the holy days must begin from sunset. This is a bone in the throat of those who disagree with us on this matter, and they have no escape from it, and this is also the case regarding what we said about the suspected adulteress. 5. Let us return to his words, according to which it is impossible that the first month should enter without its sign coming before it or together with it. [And the sign is] that the barley should be at the beginning of the month of Nisan ripe and full grains, whole, wet and congealed. And since this is so, it must be ready for harvest around the middle of the month more or less and thus it is ready for harvest on the day of the Omer, as it is said (Leviticus 23:10) "and you shall reap its harvest." In saying "its harvest" it requires that the land's harvest be natural, as it is said (Ruth 1:22) {847} "and they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest," and so it says (Joshua 3:15) "and the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the time of harvest." The saying "you shall reap its harvest" refers to this, and the intention is to natural harvest. After that he added and emphasized that this is not an action [done out of] choice in saying (Deuteronomy 16:9) "from when the sickle begins [to cut] the standing grain." He connected this to the sickle and not to us, but the sickle behaves according to nature, namely attainment, as it is said (Joel 4:13) "put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe." And he said that these are two aspects – the ripening of the grains at the beginning of the month and the harvest on the day of counting, and each aspect depends on the second, and these two days or times together encompass the [desired] state of the barley. 6. Regarding his saying that the barley must be at the beginning of the month of Nisan ripe grains, whole, full, wet and congealed and so on, we agree with him regarding the state [in which] the barley [should be]. However, [in our opinion] this necessarily happens on the thirteenth of Nisan and not at the beginning [of the month] as he claimed in the previous words. And if indeed this is so and this is on the thirteenth day then necessarily the harvest is after two or three days. And regarding his words about natural harvest, the matter is as he says, similar to what we ourselves said in the nineteenth gate 7. And he said that the quantity need not depend on the number of people, since the cause is the state [of the barley] and its form and this does not depend on people. [And this state] exists at the strongest time, which is the middle [of ripening], since at the beginning they are sparse, small and few, and at the end their strength wanes and weakens. And he said that the correct time is in the middle, and when we establish one of the components as a sign we should not rely on the small and weak that indicates the beginning of the time, which shares with the nature of what precedes this, nor [rely] on the end of ripening, since the late [grains] come only when the early ones age and wear out, and then they indicate the end of the time, which resembles the nature of the time that comes after. Rather, we search for [the time when the grains] are found in abundance and plenty, and this surely indicates the middle of the time appropriate to the nature of [ripening] time. Since this is so, we should not be satisfied with the small amount of new grain at the beginning of the month of Nisan nor with a small amount on the day of counting. And likewise [we should not be satisfied] with the other extreme, namely we should not wait until no barley remains that has not crumbled, and this happens only after the grains are ready for harvest {848} and their harvest time has already passed. Likewise, we should not wait until the day of counting to harvest such that no barley remains that is not ready for harvest. For then all that was ready for harvest at first would wither and scatter and rot and spoil. Rather, on each of the two days we must search for the middle matter, that is, the thing that has passed and scattered and spread. These are signs that enable the time that God, may He be exalted, chose and desired. One who holds to this does not turn to the number of people, since the time [is valid] by virtue of itself and by virtue of its being acted upon by the cause that activates it, except that its form is not too narrow to contain those who were commanded to fulfill the commandment [at] this [time]. And it is impossible that on the day of waving the Omer every person would be obligated in challah from the threshing floor and from the dough, but rather when the barley is widespread in every place and spreads across spaces, since it is the time that requires this and not the number of people. 8. His first words on this matter are sensible words that correspond to what we said in the eighteenth gate. However, the things he said at the end about the general rule, and the obligation of separating challah on every person, and in which he aimed to assist his teacher Anan, these contradict his previous words. 9. And he said: The response to one who thinks that the waving of the Omer occurs at the time of harvest, before or after the festival, is that the passage about Joshua and the children of Israel crossing the Jordan on the tenth of the first month refutes this. This is because the banks of the Jordan were flooded with water, and it says (Joshua 3:15) "throughout the time of harvest." And the children of Israel stayed there before they crossed, and this was on the ninth [of the month], which was the second day [of the week], since the new month was on Sunday. He mentioned their food, and that the manna ceased [to appear for them] on the fifteenth. And between Monday which is the ninth and Sunday which is the eighth there is not enough time such that on Sunday the grain would not be ready to be harvested and on Monday it would be ready for this. And if the matter were as he says then the food would have been mentioned on Sunday and the manna would have ceased [to appear] on it, but [in that this is not so] there is proof that the harvest is before Passover and that this was Sunday and they did not eat. 10. This is an irrefutable refutation, since Scripture called [the days when] the children of Israel crossed the Jordan the days of harvest, and this was after nine days had passed from the beginning of the month. And Sunday, which fell two days before the crossing, was the eighth day, and therefore it is not possible that the ninth day was counted among the days of harvest and the eighth was not. In this Scripture established a distinction between harvest and what is not harvest. And one should not establish the harvest on Sunday {849} afterward, since the difference between things becomes clear and revealed over weeks, and their state [can] reverse and their changes of form strengthen and establish themselves, as Scripture indicates regarding weeks, in which the essence of things reverses, for example in leprosy, menstruation, impurity of the dead and more. 11. This approach is absolutely fitting, and it aligns with what we believe and say, except for the proof he brought from the Joshua passage against one of our opponents. According to his words, one would have to say: if it is indeed impossible for the crop to be unfit for harvesting one day and fit for harvesting the next day, then it would be impossible for it to ever be fit for harvesting at all, since according to your words there is no day when it is unfit for harvesting that would differ from the following day. It is entirely clear that these words are refutable, and even if the unreadiness [of the crop] for harvesting disappears gradually, particularly according to what the proponent of that opinion noted regarding the weeks, it still follows that it disappears as we said – a [small] portion each day. Since this is the case, the proof is invalidated. This is because on the last day when this disappears, whether it is the seventh day or another day, the crop is not fit for harvesting, while on the eighth day after this has disappeared, it is already fit for harvesting. In the following discourse we will mention the correct proof, in the discussion about the Festival of Weeks, and the proponent of that opinion has already mentioned it, namely that the first day on which the Omer offering is waved is the first day that falls during the seven days of unleavened bread. And this follows the method of scriptural reading, as we shall indicate. 12. They further disputed with the proponent of this opinion and mentioned the search for ripening grain on the twenty-fourth of Shevat, without clarifying the [correct] meaning and in order to support and defend the opinion of the Exilarch, saying: Although the month of Nisan must be recognized by the presence of karmel (fresh grain), it is also necessary to determine whether the year should be intercalated or not before the month of Adar, for several reasons, such as [the reading of] the Megillah on Purim. And he said that if someone were to argue that this is always the twelfth month, based on the scriptural verse (Esther 3:13) "in the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar," the words of Scripture [elsewhere] contradict this (ibid. 9:31) "to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times," and also (ibid. 27) "according to their writing, and according to their appointed time." All this proves that the time of Purim and the Megillah is fixed in its proper form every year, and this form is determined by the sun or signs in the crop. And after saying "according to their appointed time," it is impossible to establish Purim in any year when the crop is unripe, and in another year when it is ripe, and in another year when it has [already become] ears of grain, for if this happens it is not "according to their appointed time," just as it is impossible for the grains and barley to be unripe in one year, complete in another year, and [ready] for harvest in a third year. Similarly, it is impossible for all the wheat to be moist during the Festival of Weeks in one year and ready for harvest in another year. Every commandment in each month has a form that is learned from signs [found] in the field and always applies to it. He added similar such statements, which need not be mentioned. 13. And the things he noted are very astonishing. It is remarkable that someone like him, despite his intelligence and wisdom, brings such proof that is unnecessary and even necessarily contradicts his previous statements that we brought in the nineteenth chapter. For we witness the changing of years and the things that happen in them that cause delays in the ripening of crops and in their being fit for harvesting after it appears and is ready for this. And if searching for spring growth in Shevat were obligatory, then this could not be changed, and the reading of the Megillah is in the twelfth month according to the scriptural verse that the proponent of that opinion cited (Esther 9:31) "in their appointed times," so there is no proof in this at all and these are empty words.

content.hebrew: תם המאמר בעזרת האל
content.english: Thus ends the discourse with God's help

content.hebrew: ברוך יוי לעולם אמן ואמן
content.english: Blessed be the Lord forever, amen and amen

content.hebrew: {851} המאמר השמיני בעניין חג השבועות שהציבור מכנה עיד אל-ענצרה, ובעניין בין הערבים, ובו חמישה עשר שערים – עשרה שערים מהם עוסקים בחג השבועות וחמישה בבין הערבים
content.english: {851} The Eighth Treatise concerning the Festival of Weeks, which the public calls Eid al-Ansara, and concerning "between the evenings," containing fifteen chapters - ten chapters dealing with the Festival of Weeks and five with "between the evenings"

content.hebrew: השער הראשון על אודות המחלוקות בעניין ראשי החודשים ודעת כל קבוצה.
content.english: The First Gate: Regarding the dispute among people concerning the day on which the Festival of Weeks falls.

content.hebrew: 1. בעניין זיהוי ראשי החודשים האומה נחלקה לשלוש קבוצות. הקבוצה האחת אמרה כי מולד הירח הוא הקובע את החודש ומהווה לו אות ובאמצעותו בלבד מזהים את ראשי החודשים. הקבוצה השנייה שללה זאת ולא ראתה בירח גורם לקביעת ראש החודש כלל. הקבוצה השלישית קבעה [את המולד כגורם] בחלק מהחודשים, אך לא בכולם, אלא מיינה אותם. 2. ואלה שקבעו את הירח כגורם לחודש נחלקו לארבע קבוצות. אחת אמרה כי הזיהוי הוא בראיית מולד הירח במערב בסוף היום, לאחר שקיעת השמש, דהיינו לאחר שהיא שקעה במערב. והזמן שבו המולד נראה הוא היום הראשון של החודש. [קבוצה זו] מחפשת את המולד החל מעשרים ותשעה יום לאחר שהוא נראה – אם הם רואים אותו [מוטב], ואם לאו החודש נעשה בן שלושים יום, והיום השלושים ואחד הוא ראש החודש הבא. זו שיטת ענן ורוב הקראים הראשונים וכל הקראים בדורנו. ויש לומר כי 'ביתום', שהזכרנו בתחילת ספר זה ואמרנו כי הוא... מצדד בדעה זו... הראשונים, בעלי... בהמשך. 3. ... המנותקים... מחבר זאת יחד עם השמש... ראש החודש, והוא מה... בראיית המולד לפני... שבו הם נוקטים עכשיו כפי שצוין... אסמאעיל אל-עֻכְּבַּרִי [=ישמעאל העכברי] ומוסא אל-זעפראני, [ובתחילה] צידד בזה גם דניאל אל-קומסי לפני שהוא [עבר] לצדד בראיית המולד. {791} כך גם כל הקראים הראשונים מבצרה ומחֻ'רַאסַאן. והם מבינים את המולד כזמן שבו הירח נפרד מהשמש, וכאילו הוא 'נולד'. ויש ביניהם שתי דעות בעניין: יש הטוענים כי כאשר פרידה זו מתרחשת בין תחילת היום עד מאה ארבעים ואחת דקות מהשעה השישית, שזה חצות היום, יום זה הוא ראש החודש. אולם אם היא מתרחשת אפילו דקה אחת לאחר מכן ראש החודש חל ביום שלמחרת, וזאת משום [שזמן] הקורבן כבר חלף. 4. אחרים מתוכם אמרו כי אין זה משנה באיזה זמן ביום מתרחשת [אותה פרידה], ויום זה הוא ראש החודש אף אם נותרה רק דקה אחת [לסוף] היום. זאת משום שלא ייתכן כי היום שבו הגורם לחידוש החודש מתממש [ייחשב] ישן. זו שיטת אסמאעיל אל-עכברי ואל-תפליסי. הם סבורים כי החודש נמשך עשרים ותשעה ימים ושתים עשרה שעות ושבע מאות ותשעים ושלוש דקות, וכאשר זמן זה עובר החודש מסתיים ומתחיל החודש הבא. ויש אומרים כי זו גם שיטת השומרונים והם טוענים כי הם המוסרים [שיטה זו]...
content.english: 1. All Jewish sects called Karaites - [those attributed] to Anan, Benjamin, Ismail al-Ukbari, al-Tiflisi, al-Ramli, Daniel al-Qumisi, as well as our contemporaries who are not associated with any particular methodology - [among all these] there is no dispute that the day of waving the Omer is on Sunday and no other day of the week, and that this ends on Saturday, which is the end of the seven weeks. Then the fiftieth day, which is the Festival of Weeks, also falls on Sunday. However, the Rabbanites disagree with this and argue that the day of waving the Omer is on the sixteenth of Nisan, regardless of which day of the week it falls on, and on that same [day of the week after seven weeks] falls the Festival of Weeks. 2. Those who advocate for Sunday [of the week] are divided among themselves - the majority, as well as the masses, say that the Sunday which is the day of waving the Omer and on which the counting of weeks begins is the one that comes immediately after the Passover sacrifice, and it must be one of the seven days of Passover - neither before nor after them. However, some of the early Karaites of Basra disagreed with this, and Meshuyah al-Ukbari followed them. They argued that this Sunday is not fixed, but rather it may come either before or after the seven days of Passover, and it depends on a certain action which is the beginning of the harvest, and it may come before [Passover] or after it. And some of these people, unlike the rest of the nation in the East and West, did not require celebrating the Festival of Weeks in the diaspora. In the following discussion, we will present their arguments on this matter.

content.hebrew: השער השלישי על אודות דברו (בראשית א:יד) 'והיו לאותות ולמועדים' ועל אודות כך שהירח הוא הגורם והאות [לקביעת] החודש.
content.english: The Second Gate: Regarding our colleagues' argument that the day of waving the Omer is exclusively on {853} Sunday.

content.hebrew: 1. וזה כמו... הבטחתו. והכוונה בדבר התורה 'במועדים' אינה... מועדים, שכן משמעות זו אינה מתאימה כאן. אלא המשמעות של זה קשורה בוודאי לאחד משני החלקים האחרים, דהיינו או שהוא התכוון לזמנים ולעיתים או [שהוא התכוון] לחגים, ואין אפשרות אחרת. [והאות] ו' בדברו' מועדים' מבוטלת, כפי שביארנו במקומות אחרים כי בתורה [יש מופעים של האות] ו' שבהם היא מבוטלת. דוגמה לכך היא (במדבר ד:יט) 'וזאת עשו להם וחיו', ואין צורך [באות] ו' [במילה] 'וזאת'. וכמו כן (שם ז:יג) 'וקרבנו קערת כסף'. והכוונה בדברו 'והיו לאותות ולמועדים' היא כי שני המאורות האלה הם השמש והירח, שהם סימנים וציונים למועדים, שהם הזמנים והעיתים או החגים. 2. {792} אם המשמעות היא זמנים ועיתים הרי יש שלושה מקטעים וחלוקות של זמן. האחד הוא החלוקה בין יום ליום, השני בין חודש לחודש והשלישי בין שנה לשנה. החלוקה בין ימים ברורה וגלויה לכל אדם, שכן בעת שקיעת השמש יוצא יום ונכנס יום אחר, ועל כך נאמר (בראשית א:ה וכו') 'ויהי ערב ויהי בקר יום'. גם החלוקה בין שנה לשנה היא על פי השמש בלבד, ונבאר זאת בהמשך, ועל כל נאמר (דברים לג:יד) 'וממגד תבואות שמש'. ומאחר שהוא הודיע כי שני המאורות האלה, השמש והירח, הם הסימנים לזמנים ועל פיהם נעשית החלוקה בין זמן לזמן, והחלוקה לשמנים היא משולשת כפי שביארנו, ומאחר שהתאמת כי שתי חלוקות הן על פי השמש, הרי שהנותר, דהיינו הסימן השלישי שהוא החלוקה בין חודש לחודש, ייעשה בהכרח על פי הירח בלבד. מזה התאמת כי הירח הוא הגורם [הקובע] את החודש... חודש מחודש. וכן אף אם משמעות דברו 'מועדים' היא חגים מתברר כי לשמש אין תפקיד בקביעת החודש כלל, שכן החגים חלים בתאריכים מסוימים בחודש. לכן מסתמן כי [החודש נקבע] על פי הירח בלבד. 3. ואל-פיומי טען כי דברו (בראשית א:יד) מתייחס לדברו (שם שם) 'בין היום ובין הלילה', וכי היום והלילה הם 'לאותות ולמועדים' ולא המאורות. תשובה אחת לטענתו היא בדברו (שם שם) 'ולימים', שהרי מדברו יוצא כי הימים הם סימנים לימים, וזו טענה בלתי הגיונית וחסרת פשר. וכן דברו (תהלים קד:יט) 'עשה ירח למועדים' מחזק את שיטתנו. תשובה נוספת לדברו היא כי היום והלילה נבראו לפני המאורות, ולכן אילו דברו 'והיו לאותות' היה מתייחס לדברו 'בין היום ובין הלילה' הוא היה מזכיר זאת כבר מעת בריאת היום והלילה. מזה נודע כי דברו 'לאותות' וכו' מתייחס אך ורק למאורות. 4. הוכחה לכך שהירח הוא הגורם [לקביעת] החודש והוא הסימן והאות שלו היא כי החודש נקרא אחריו, כדברו (שמות ב:ב) 'ותצפנהו שלושה ירחים', וכן (מלכים א ו:לא) '[ב]ירח בול', (שם לז) '[ב]ירח זיו', (שם ח:ב) '[ב]ירח האיתנים'. וזו גם משמעות דברו בתורה (דברים לג:יד) 'וממגד תבואות שמש וממגד גרש ירחים'. הכוונה בדברו 'תבואות שמש' היא כפשוטו – התבואה שעולה כל שנה ושנה באמצעות תנועת [השמש] והשפעתה עליה. והכוונה בדברו 'גרש ירחים' היא לתבואה שתהיה כאשר יבוא {793} המשיח, שתעלה כל חודש וחודש, כדברו (יחזקאל מז:יב) 'לחדשיו יבכר'. והחודש מכונה ירח משום שהירח הוא הגורם (לקביעתו) והוא הסימן והאות שלו. ואילו היה מישהו אומר כי זה ידוע מתוך הכרח, היו [דבריו] נכוחים, ומי שהיה מתכחש לזה... 5. ... 'אות' בכך שהוא ברור, מוחשי וגלוי לעין. וכן ראינו כי זו דרכה של השמש וכי גם היא אות, שכן היא מוחשית וגלויה לעין. לכן גם הירח צריך להיות אות, שכן הוא מוחשי וגלוי לעין. ומישהו עשוי לחלוק עלינו באמצעות דבר התורה על אודות השבת (שמות לא:יג) 'כי אות היא', שהרי זו אינה גלויה לעין. התשובה לזה היא כי השבת היא יום, וכל הימים הם גלויים לעין בכך שאור השמש זורח ושוקע. תשובה נוספת היא כי הוא לא אמר כי השבת היא אות באופן מוחלט, אלא אמר: היא אות ביני וביניכם, כדי שייוודע כי אני האל מקדשכם. וייתכן כי הכוונה בזה היא [לאות] שאנשים רואים בכך שאתם שובתים [ביום] זה וכך הם יודעים כי אני מגן בה עליכם, וכך משמעות [המילה] אות [בהקשר זה] היא השביתה. 6. ואחד מחברינו אמר כי אין צורך להביא הוכחה לכך שראש החודש נקבע על ידי ראיית הירח, שכן כאשר משה עליו השלום אמר לבני ישראל בשם הבורא יתעלה (בראשית א:יד) 'והיו לאותות' הוא הודיע בזה כי הירח הוא אות לחודש ולמועדים, והוא לא [ראה] צורך לבאר להם איך זה קורה ובאיזה אופן, משום שהם כבר היו מורגלים בכך במורשה [שהגיעה אליהם] מעת תחילת הבריאה וראשית ההוויה. [דהיינו מורגלים בכך] שהחודש, שנקרא ירח, מתחיל בעת התחדשות הירח ועלייתו לאחר שנסתר. וזה היה בתפיסתם כדבר ראשוני בשכל [שהוא מובן מאליו], אין בו ספק או מחלוקת ואיש אינו מתכחש לו כך שיהיה צורך בהוכחה או במופת. זה דומה לאדם שהולך בדרך ישרה בדרכו אל מקום מסוים, והוא הולך מתוך כוונה ידועה ובאופן שהוא בקיא בו ואין נכנס [בליבו] חשד או ספק, ובעוד הוא הולך ניצבים לפני אנשים ושואלים אותו: לאן אתה פונה בדרכך? הוא עונה: אל מקום פלוני. הם אומרים: הדרך שבה אתה הולך לא תוביל אותך אל מחוז חפצך ולא תוליך אותך אל מבוקשך, טעית וסרת מעל הדרך הראשית. אומר להם האיש: איך אלך כדי להגיע אל מקום חפצי ואשיג את מבוקשי? אחד מהם אומר: פנה לימין, אחר אומר: לא, אלא פנה לשמאל, ואחר אומר: חזור אחורה אל מקום פלוני, [ושם] תלך בדרך פלונית. וכאשר האיש שומע {794} את הדעות השונות סרה ממנו הוודאות שהייתה לו והוא מתמלא מחשד ובספק, והוא נקלע למבוכה על אודות מצבו, ואז הוא מבקש הוכחה שתאשש את אחת הדעות שניתנו לו. ואילו הוא היה נותר במצבו הראשון והולך בכיוון שבו הלך בתחילה הוא היה מגיע אל מחוז חפצו האמיתי. 7. [ואותו חבר] אמר: כך גם היה מצב האומה בעניין מולד הירח – הם נהגו בזה על פי מסורת ישרה שאינה דורשת מופת או הוכחה, וכאשר החלו הניגודים ורבו הדעות וכל קבוצה הלכה בדרך [אחרת] ואימצה לעצמה שיטה היה צורך להבחין בין השיטות הללו ולבטל את [השיטה] הנפסדת ולאמת את הנכונה. וההוכחה לאמיתות דעה זו היא מה שמקובל בידינו מספרי הרבניים כי ראיית המולד היא האות לחודש וכי ליל המולד הוא ראש החודש. ומדבריהם ברור כי זה היה להם כטבע שאין בו חשד או ספק, ונדון בזה במקומו כפי שזה כתוב במשנה. עוד יותר בולט מזה הוא כי הם אמרו בכמה מאמרותיהם כי כאשר הבורא יתעלה אמר למשה עליו השלום (שמות יב:ב) 'החדש הזה לכם ראשי חדשים' הוא הצביע על המולד ואמר לו 'החדש הזה', כלומר זהו סימן החודש ותחילתו, כפי שאמרנו קודם בשמם כי הם מכנים את הירח 'חודש'. 8. וכמה מחברינו הביאו הוכחה [לקביעת המולד על פי] ראייה על ידי פסילה. הכוונה בזה היא כי כל מי שטוען [שיש לקבוע] את ראש החודש שלא על ידי ראייה טועה בדברו, ומאחר שכך הדבר וכל הדעות החולקות על הראייה נפסדות הרי הדעה המצדדת בראייה היא הנותרת ולכן היא הנכונה. ונבאר כיצד כל הדעות שחולקות על הראייה נפסדות.
content.english: 1. The Torah said (Leviticus 23:15) "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Sabbath, from the day you bring" etc., and also (ibid.) "seven complete Sabbaths shall there be." It also said (ibid. 16) "until the morrow of the seventh Sabbath shall you count fifty days." It connected this to two days, both of which it called 'Sabbath'. If the first is considered a festival, then the second must also be considered as such. If the intention in its first statement 'the morrow of the Sabbath' meant the day after the festival, then it would necessarily follow that before the Festival of Weeks there must be a festival day that the Festival of Weeks follows on the morrow, and this is refuted as there is no such festival. The Rabbanites established the [meaning of the] first [verse] as the day after the festival and the second as the day after the Sabbath in a way that contains a contradiction, and claimed there is a difference between the words even though they are identical. Some [of the Rabbanites] said something else which we will discuss later. What we have said is only one consideration. 2. Another consideration is that the definite article 'hey' in the Torah's words (Leviticus 23:15) 'the Sabbath' refers to the known and familiar Sabbath and not to a festival or any other day. This is because festivals mentioned in a similar manner, such as Yom Kippur, are referred to as (ibid. 32) "a Sabbath of complete rest" (shabbat shabbaton), and not as 'the Sabbath' with the definite article, [and the definite form] indicates only the [familiar] Sabbath and nothing else. And so too with Sukkot, about which it is said (ibid. 39) "on the first day shall be a solemn rest." We do not find that He called any of these days 'the Sabbath' except for the familiar and designated Sabbath. Moreover, in saying 'the Sabbath' He surely referred to a specific day that is known and familiar, and we do not find any known and familiar day previously mentioned except the Sabbath. 3. And someone might dispute this, in light of His words in Ezekiel (Ezekiel 46:12) "Now when the prince shall prepare a freewill-offering, a burnt-offering or peace-offerings" etc., and also (ibid.) "and he shall prepare his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings, as he does on the Sabbath day." And since it is forbidden to offer peace-offerings on the Sabbath, therefore the intention in saying 'on the Sabbath day' must surely refer to the festival day. There are two answers to this objection - one is that {854} which our colleagues rely upon, according to which the intention of the words 'as he does' does not refer to the sacrifice but rather to the previous words (ibid.) "and one shall open for him the gate," as afterwards it says "as he does on the Sabbath day and he shall go out, and shut the gate." And similarly it says elsewhere (ibid. 1) "the gate of the inner court" etc., and also (ibid.) "and on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened." From this it is confirmed that His words "and he shall do as he does on the Sabbath day" refer to the opening of the gate, which is customarily done on the Sabbath day without sacrifice. 4. The other answer is that He informed that on the Sabbath the prince has a special obligatory offering that is different from the offering of the rest of the nation, which is (Ezekiel 46:4) "six lambs." And in saying (ibid. 12) "as he does on the Sabbath day" the intention is that he shall offer his voluntary burnt-offering as he offers his special burnt-offering on the Sabbath day. A third [possible] answer is from His words (Leviticus 23:16) "the seventh," for if in saying 'the Sabbath' the intention was to the festival, then it would necessarily follow that there would be seven festivals before the Festival of Weeks, or that it would be the seventh. And there is no need to explain the corruption of this idea.

content.hebrew: השער הרביעי על אודות דעת הצדוקים והמענה אליהם.
content.english: The Third Gate: Regarding the presentation of arguments by one who adopts the Rabbanite view that the day of waving the Omer is on the sixteenth of Nisan.

content.hebrew: 1. אנו מזכירים אותם בראשונה משום שהם הראשונים בין כל הקבוצות. וכבר אמרנו כי לשיטתם כל החודשים הם בני שלושים [ימים]. כראיה לכך הם הביאו את סיפור נח וזה שהוא הודיע שם כי חמישה חודשים {795} הם מאה וחמישים ימים. ואולם את השיטה הזו מבטלת [העובדה] כי הירח הוא הגורם [לקביעת] החודש, שאותה איששנו בהוכחות מופתיות, כי [הירח] הוא לבדו האות שהרי החודש כונה ירח, וכי הוא אומר (בראשית א:יד) 'והיו לאותות ולמועדים', וכן (תהלים קד:יט) 'עשה ירח למועדים', וכן [יש הוכחות] נוספות. ובאשר [לראיה] שהם נסמכים עליה בסיפור נח, זה מתרחש בהכרח כאשר הירח אינו עולה, וכאשר השמיים נקיים מעננים יש לחפש את המולד בלילה השלושים. אם הוא נראה [יום זה] הוא ראש החודש ואם הוא לא נראה או שהיו עננים שהסתירו אותו ראש החודש הוא ביום השלושים ואחד. 2. ההוכחה לזה היא בטבע שקבע האל לירח [ובכורח] שבריאתו כופה עליו בכך שהוא תמיד מופיע באחת משני לילות אלה, כלומר הוא אינו מופיע לפני הלילה השלושים ולא אחרי הלילה השלושים ואחד. ומאחר שכך הדבר ואין בזה שינוי עלינו לחפש את [המולד] בלילה הראשון, דהיינו השלושים, כאשר יש בידינו לראותו, ואם איננו רואים אותו אנו קובעים אותו ביום השלושים ואחד [ובשלב זה כבר] איננו צריכים לחפש אותו, בין אם יש עננים ובין אם לאו, שכן הוא בהכרח הופיע בלילה זה. וחמשת החודשים בסיפור נח הם מאה וחמישים יום, וזה אינו מתאים לשיטות של מרבית חברינו ונדון בזה בהמשך. 3. [הוכחה] נוספת לביטול דעת הצדוקים מצויה בחיוב שהאל חייב אותנו בעניין האביב, בדברו (דברים טז:א) 'שמור את חדש האביב', שעל זה התנהלה בדורות קודמים חקירה, כי בחלק מהשנים יש שניים עשר חודשים ובחלק שלושה עשר, שהן השנים המעוברות. והחקירה קבעה כי בכל תשע עשרה שנים יהיו שבע שנים מעוברות, כפי שציינו הרבניים בעניין המחזור שלא הייתה מחלוקת לגביו במשך אלף ושלוש מאות שנים בקירוב. ואם מקדימים את אחת השנים או מאחרים אותה [בתוך המסגרת של תשע עשרה השנים] אין בכך הבדל. ובאותו אופן הדבר נוהג גם באשר לחודשי השנה ובטבע הופעת הירח והיעלמו כפי שקבע לו האל, שכן בדרך כלל בשנה בת שניים עשר חודשים יש שלוש מאות חמישים וחמישה ימים. ואם תוציא את שבעת החודשים המעוברים מתוך תשע עשרה השנים הללו ותחלק את מאתיים ועשרת הימים שיש בהם על פני תשע עשרה השנים בכל שנה יהיו אחד עשר ימים, וכך בכל שנה יהיו בסך הכול שלוש מאות שישים ושישה ימים, שזו {796} שנת השמש, שעל פיה סובבות שנות השמש. ואילו לפי הצדוקים, שטוענים כי בכל חודשי השנה יש שלושים ימים, כך שבכל שנה יש שלוש מאות ושישים ימים – לא יותר ולא פחות, השנה קצרה יותר משנת השמש, שהחקירה קבעה כי על פיו נקבע האביב, בשישה ימים בשנה, כך [שביחס לשנת השמש] היא מחסירה חודש אחד כל חמש שנים. כך, כל שלושים שנה ייווצר בין שנת השמש לשנה שלהם [פער] של שישה חודשים וכאשר אצלנו חל ניסן אצלם יחול תשרי, ויבטל החיוב באביב ובעומר, בניגוד לדברי התורה. 4. והבורא יתעלה הגדיר בעניין החגים שלושה דברים המבטלים את דעת הצדוקים. האחד הוא עניין האביב והעומר שחג המצות תלוי בו, כפי שהזכרנו. השני הוא חג השבועות, שעליו הוא כתב במפורש שהוא צריך להתקיים בתחילת קציר החיטה, בדברו (שמות לד:כב) 'וחג שבועות תעשה לך בכורי קציר חטים'. וכך גם נהוג, והחקירה צדקה בזה, כי בין קציר השעורה לתחילת קציר החיטה יש כשלושה ימים. השלישי הוא בדברו על אודות חג הסוכות (שם כג:טז) 'באספך את מעשיך'. ודבר זה גלוי תמיד לעין, כי בתשרי נכנסים כל הפירות. וכבר אמרנו כי כל הצדוקים מחייבים כך יהיה בכל החודשים ואפילו בניסן. ונפסדוּת דבריהם ברורה מכל כיוון.
content.english: 1. He said that the first festival that the Children of Israel were commanded about was Passover and the seven days of unleavened bread, and thirty days after celebrating the days of unleavened bread they were commanded about the Sabbath while they were (Numbers 33:13) in "Alush" and there they observed it for the first time, on the twenty-second of the month of Iyar. And he said that Passover occurs at three times, the first being the time of its slaughter on the fourteenth [of Nisan] and also on the morrow of that day on the fifteenth, and this is the intention of the verse (ibid. 3) "And they journeyed from Rameses to Succoth in the first month, on the fifteenth," and also the verse (ibid.) "on the morrow of the Passover." And the {855} second time is the time of eating on the fifteenth, at the beginning of the night, as it says (Exodus 12:8) "and they shall eat the flesh in that night." And the proof that this is the fifteenth day is that the entire night is counted together with the day that follows it as one day. And the morrow of the day on which the Passover is eaten is the sixteenth [of the month]. 2. And the third time is the time of the passing over, and it is more important than the previous times, because they [exist] due to it and are named after it. And the time of the passing over is from midnight of the fifteenth, as it says (Exodus 12:27) "you shall say: It is the Passover sacrifice unto the Lord," and this is on the fourteenth. And the passing over was at the time of the smiting, as it says (ibid.) "who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when He smote the Egyptians." And the smiting was at midnight, as it says (ibid. 29) "And it came to pass at midnight that the Lord smote all the firstborn." And the morrow of that day was the sixteenth, and the fifteenth is Passover. And the slaughter [of the Passover] is on the fourteenth because its eating is on the fifteenth, and the day after is the sixteenth. And he said this is the reason why we say that Passover occurs at three times and that the third of them is the most important, because in it lies the original purpose. 3. And he said: Reinforcement that the sixteenth day is the morrow of Passover is found in the story of Joshua, in the verse (Joshua 5:11) "And they did eat of the produce of the land on the morrow of the Passover, unleavened cakes and parched corn," as it is said in the Torah (Leviticus 23:14) "And ye shall eat neither bread, nor parched corn, nor fresh ears, until this selfsame day," and this is after both times of Passover - the time of eating and the time about which it is said (Exodus 12:27) "who passed over the houses of the children of Israel." And this is [another] reason. 4. And he said: If the matter were as those who oppose [my opinion] claim, [and the Omer] was on the fifteenth and this was Sunday, when would they reap, thresh, winnow and grind? For the fifteenth day is a holy convocation and these labors are forbidden on it. From this it is proven that that day was a weekday and these labors were permitted on it. And if they claim that they reaped and performed these labors before the Sabbath began, this is a corrupt argument, for this day would [already] be the thirteenth, and it is forbidden to present a harvest for an offering two days before [the offering itself], in light of the verse (Leviticus 23:10) "the first of your harvest." And if they reaped on the thirteenth for their needs and on the fifteenth for the offering, this is not the first of the harvest, {856} and if they reaped on the thirteenth for the Omer then it is invalid, like a peace-offering that is piggul (unfit). 5. And he said: Another proof is that a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment, for example that a sacrifice or circumcision override the prohibition of labor on the Sabbath. And if there is an obligation to wave the Omer on a holy convocation day then it is permitted to reap, thresh, winnow and grind on this day, [these being labors] which are inherently forbidden. And further he said that from the verse (Deuteronomy 16:6) "the season of thy coming forth out of Egypt" [we learn] that they did not depart at sunset, for He says to them (Exodus 12:22) "and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning." And the intention of the words "the season of thy coming forth" refers to the seven days of unleavened bread, for the seven days are a memorial to the exodus from Egypt, as it says (Deuteronomy 16:3) "Thou shalt eat no leavened bread with it; seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread therewith, even the bread of affliction" etc. 6. And he said: Another consideration indicates that the intention of the verse (Deuteronomy 16:6) "at sunset" refers to the night of the sixteenth. This is because on the morning of the fifteenth they went to the edge of the city of Rameses, sat there and completed [there] the festival until the end of the day. And they went to the edge of the city because they were expelled, and in this departure it is not mentioned that they camped. The proof for this is in the verse (Exodus 12:39) "And they baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought forth out of Egypt." And if the dough had been on their shoulders from Rameses to Succoth, which is a day's journey, it would have become leavened. And at sunset of the fifteenth day on the night of the sixteenth it is said "at sunset." 7. And further he said that in the verse (Deuteronomy 16:8) "six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread" the intention is that the first day on which they departed is the fifteenth, for on the morrow on the sixteenth He said (ibid. 7) "and thou shalt turn in the morning, and go," and afterward He said "six days," which begin on the sixteenth, and the seventh is a solemn assembly. And he said: Another consideration is that on the first day, which is the fifteenth, eating of new grain was forbidden, and therefore it is excluded from the seven, and there remain six days in which it is permitted to eat new grain. These are his words as they [were said], and I have not omitted anything from them, but rather, I have strengthened them through quality phrasing.

content.hebrew: השער החמישי על אודות טענת אנשי המערה לזיהוי הירח המלא.
content.english: The Fourth Gate: Regarding the refutation of this view.

content.hebrew: 1. הם טענו כי בתחילת הבריאה האל ישתבח ברא את כל הגופים שלמים וגמורים. כך היו אדם וחוה וכן החיות – את כולם הוא ברא שלמים בגופם. וכך גם באשר לצמחים, כגון העצים. וכך הוא ברא גם את עצם שני המאורות – השמש והירח – וכן את שאר הכוכבים בשיא השלמות. כהוכחה לכך שהירח נברא שלם וגמור הם הביאו את דברו (תהלים פט:לח) 'כירח יכון עולם', [כלומר] כפי שהעולם נברא שלם וגמור כך גם היה הירח שלם בעת בריאתו. וכן הם אמרו כי התורה כינתה את שני המאורות בעת בריאתם {797} (בראשית א:טז) '[ה]גדולים', וזה היה ביום הרביעי, שאין מחלוקת על כך שהוא היה ראש החודש וכי הם נבראו בשיא גודלם, שכן הוא כינה אותם 'גדולים'. והירח הוא בשיא גודלו בעת היותו מלא, ומזה אנו למדים כי היום שבו הוא מלא הוא ראש החודש.
content.english: 1. {857} There is no need to mention what he wrote at the beginning of his words, but our intention is to mention his words regarding the passing over, that it was on the fifteenth, and that the morrow [of Passover] was the sixteenth day. We say: He referred us to the scripture, according to which the morrow of Passover is the fifteenth day. And his second argument is a corrupt argument that has no demonstrative proof, because every 'morrow' that is mentioned refers to the night that preceded it, and the Torah says that this is from the morrow of the night that was not preceded by [another] night or day. Proof for this is in the words of the Torah (Numbers 11:32) "And the people stood up all that day, and all the night, and all the next day," they began gathering at the beginning of the day until its end and then at night and on the day after that night. And the term 'morrow' applies to the day after this night, and this cannot be denied, and we do not find anything in the Torah that contradicts this. The Torah says that the fifteenth is the morrow of Passover and elsewhere it says that the day that comes immediately after the night is the morrow to it, and from this it is confirmed that the fifteenth is the morrow of Passover without doubt, and his claim that the morrow of Passover is the sixteenth is nullified. 2. And regarding the evidence that he sought from the story of Joshua and his question about when they reaped and threshed and winnowed and ground, this is difficult also on the sixteenth [of the month], since the things he mentioned cannot be performed in an hour or two, not in half a day and not even in two or three days. And in our opinion, it is possible that they found grain in granaries that had been emptied of the harvest, threshing and grinding. And it is also possible [that the grain they found] was not ground and they ground and baked it on the fifteenth day and then ate it. It is also possible that they did all these actions on the thirteenth and ate on the fifteenth day. 3. And regarding his words about the Omer, the Torah obligated us to wave the Omer from our own harvest and not from that of others, as it says (Leviticus 23:10) "and ye shall reap," and afterward (ibid.) "then ye shall bring the sheaf of the first of your harvest." He strengthened this in two ways, one is His saying "and ye shall reap," and the second is "your harvest." This does not include the harvest of others. And it is possible that they ate what they saw had been completed in its preparation, and they found [grain] that had not been reaped, and they reaped from it for the Omer on the thirteenth day and offered from it on the fifteenth. 4. And regarding his statement that this is invalid and that {858} it follows the way of peace offerings which on the third day become piggul (unfit), this cannot be so because grain and sheaves do not behave like meat, since meat changes and spoils while sheaves do not change or spoil. And the Torah commanded us to bring the first of our harvest, but did not specify that this must be on the same day or at the same hour, and therefore we are permitted to bring this even after a day or two due to constraint or necessity. 5. And we have already shown before that his statement that positive commandments override negative commandments is invalid. And likewise [we have shown this] regarding his statement that it is forbidden for them to reap and thresh and winnow their grain on that same day, and we have already discussed this at the beginning of this chapter. And regarding his argument concerning the verse (Deuteronomy 16:6) "the season of thy coming forth out of Egypt" that their departure was not at that time, meaning in the evening, this argument does not affect us and causes no damage to our method but rather [on the contrary], it [fits us] and strengthens our words. 6. And regarding his statement that they departed on the morning of the fifteenth and that the verse (Deuteronomy 16:6) "at sunset" refers to the sunset of the fifteenth day, meaning on the night of the sixteenth, in all this there is blindness of heart regarding a case that has no substance, since according to his words "at sunset" precedes his words (ibid.) "thou shalt sacrifice the passover-offering in the evening." His words "at sunset" refer to the Passover sacrifice that preceded it. And if it were as he says, the Passover sacrifice would have to be on the night of the sixteenth, which is foolishness and ignorance. And if his intention was that the meaning of "at sunset" refers to what comes after (ibid.) "the season of thy coming forth out of Egypt," and that their departure was on the night of the sixteenth, then [even then] this contradicts his previous words, according to which the intention in the verse "the season of thy coming forth out of Egypt" refers to all seven days and not to this specific time. 7. And regarding his initial words, that they went to the edge of the city and camped there until the end of the festival, this is what we also claim. But his words about (Deuteronomy 16:8) "six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread," that the first day is the fifteenth day, these contradict what necessarily follows from the scripture, since six [days] are mentioned and then He informed about a seventh [day], saying "six days thou shalt eat unleavened bread" and then (ibid.) "and on the seventh day shall be a solemn assembly to the Lord thy God." He made a distinction between the sixth and the seventh, which is a solemn assembly, whose meaning {859} according to the Torah is restraint and a place of confinement and so forth. And this is unlike the previous six days, to which this matter does not apply. And his words that the fifteenth is excluded from the seven [days] because eating new grain is forbidden on it are among his baseless claims and they themselves constitute a contradiction and dispute. 8. The sum of the matter is that the Torah explicitly states that the fifteenth is the morrow of Passover and on it Israel departed from Egypt, as it says (Numbers 33:3) "And they journeyed from Rameses." He mentioned a journey and then informed that this journey took place on the fifteenth, saying (ibid.) "on the fifteenth day." Then He informed that the fifteenth was the morrow of Passover. Afterward He returned and emphasized this by connecting the departure with the morrow of Passover, saying (ibid.) "on the morrow of the passover they went out." All this is continuous speech that is not interrupted from its beginning with "And they journeyed" until its end, which is (ibid.) "in the sight of all the Egyptians," and everything refers to one day and one time. And this is a bone in their throat [of those who disagree] and they have no escape, except through confusion and disruption of the scriptures from their order by dividing them into two contrary to the words of the Torah. His words "And they journeyed from Rameses... on the fifteenth" they interpret as referring to one matter, which is the first departure, and His words "on the morrow of the passover they went out" to another matter, which is another departure on another day. Thus they did also regarding (Leviticus 23:15) "[from] the morrow of the sabbath" the first [which they interpreted as referring to] the morrow of the festival, and His words (ibid. 16) "until the morrow of the sabbath" the second [which they interpreted as referring to] the morrow of the Sabbath. [And this is something] (Deuteronomy 18:21) "which the Lord hath not spoken." Afterward they contradicted this by claiming that His words "until the morrow of the seventh sabbath" refers to the week, contrary to what necessarily follows from the context and the language. 9. Support for our words and for the fact that the exodus from Egypt was on a distinguished, honored and mighty day, is found in His words (Exodus 12:51) "And it came to pass the selfsame day that the Lord did bring" etc., and also (ibid. 41) "[And it came to pass at the end of] that all the hosts of the Lord went out" etc. This could only have been on the fifteenth day, which alone is a holy convocation. 10. Additional support for this comes from the fact that all festivals are defined and described [as occurring] on a specific day in a specific month, [a date] that cannot be moved earlier or later, except for the day of waving the Omer and the festival of Shavuot. This is decisive proof that they do not have a fixed date in the month, contrary to their claim that the day of waving the Omer is the sixteenth of Nisan and cannot deviate from this, and that the festival of Shavuot is on the sixth {860} of Sivan and cannot deviate from this. If it were as they claim, he would have defined [these festivals] and explained [their dates] just as he defined and explained the rest [of the festivals]. Even if we assume that mention of one of the festivals was [simply] omitted, [for example] the day of waving the Omer, how is it that mention of Shavuot was also omitted? This surely proves that the matter is not as they said, but rather both festivals depend on the morrow of the Sabbath.

content.hebrew: השער השישי על אודות דחיית [דבריהם].
content.english: The Fifth Gate: Concerning the Presentation of Arguments That Others Bring to Prove Their Position

content.hebrew: 1. הדבר הראשון שמכריע אותם ומפריך את דבריהם הוא דבר התורה שהזכרנו קודם (במדבר כח:יד) 'זאת עולת חדש בחדשו'. ופירוש דברו 'בחדשו' הוא כאשר הוא מתחדש, והכוונה בזה היא חידוש הירח, שכן החודש נקרא ירח. ואין דרכו של דבר שהיה חסר והושלם או שנוסף לו [דבר מה] להיקרא חדש, אלא בכל הלשונות דבר חדש הוא שלא היה ואז נוצר מתוך האין או הופיע מתוך ההיעדר. ואם כך הוא הדבר הרי דברם כי ראש החודש חל בליל הירח המלא מתבטל שכן [הירח] מופיע ונמצא עוד לפני הלילה ההוא. והוא בהכרח מתחדש בלילה שבו הוא מופיע במערב לאחר ששקע במזרח, ולכן אילו הוא היה [נחשב] חדש בליל הירח המלא משום שצורתו גדלה מכפי שהייתה קודם לכן הרי שהוא היה צריך להיחשב כחדש בכל לילה מעת שיצא ועד ללילה הארבעה עשר, שכן בכל אחד מהלילות הללו צורתו משתנה וגופו גדל. אולם זה בלתי אפשרי ומשום כך בטל דברם כי ראש החודש חל בליל הירח המלא לפי דבר התורה 'בחדשו'. 2. ויש להגיד להם: לפי טענתכם כי כל דבר שהאל בורא נברא כאשר גופו שלם, האם אתם מוצאים בכל הבריאה איזושהי חיה או צמח [שכבר] בתחילת בריאתם הם בשיא שלמותם? הרי כל דבר שקיים ומתהווה בעולם הוא קטן ודק בתחילתו ואז מוסיף וגדל עד שהוא משיג את קצו. ומאחר שכך הדבר, בהכרח גם הירח והחודש נוהגים כך – בתחילתו [הירח] הוא {798} קטן ואז הוא מוסיף וגדל עד שהוא נשלם כשהוא מלא. [זמן זה הוא זמן] האמצע, שממנו והלאה הוא מצטמצם עד שהוא נעלם מהעין. 3. ובאשר לפסוק שהם הביאו (תהלים פט:לח) 'כירח יכון עולם', הם פירשו אותו באופן מוטעה, שכן מדובר בדוד ובהבטחת האל יתעלה אליו כי מלכותו תשב לנצח. שכן בתחילה הוא אומר (שם כא) 'מצאתי דוד עבדי' והוא ממשיך לספר על אודותיו עד לדברו (שם לז) 'זרעו לעולם יהיה', ואז הוא אמר כירח יכון עולם'. והוא הודיע בזה כי זרעו ומלכותו ישבו לנצח כמו השמש והירח. ואין כאן תיאור לירח שנברא שלם או חסר. 4. ובאשר לפסוק שהם הביאו לראיה (בראשית א:טז) 'הגדולים', אין בכוונה בזה לגודל גופם, שכן יש כוכבים הגדולים בגופם מהירח. אלא הכוונה לעוצמת אורם, שכן אורם גדול יותר משל כל הכוכבים. ואין ספק כי בדרך כלל אור הירח וכן גופו בלילה הראשון לצאתו במערב הם גדולים ועוצמתיים יותר [מאור] כל הכוכבים [וגודל גופם], ואין להסיק מזה כי גם בלילה הראשון לבריאתו הוא בשיא גודלו ועוצמת אורו. 5. עוד יש להגיד להם: האין זה מתחייב כי בליל ראש החודש יהיה הירח בעל צורה השונה מזו שבשאר לילות החודש? [התשובה] היא בהכרח חיובית, שאם לא כן היה עניינו מסופק ומהותו לא הייתה נודעת. ושתי הדעות הן נפסדות, שהרי אנו רואים מה מצבו של הירח בלילות השני והשלישי לחודש מעת [הופעת] הירח המלא, ומאחר שזה דרכו [של הירח] זה מפריך את הדעה שלפיה מילוי הירח הוא סימן לתחילת החודש.
content.english: 1. This [person] took some of our words and arguments and clung to them, arguing regarding the opinion that Shavuot [falls] only on Sunday, such that sometimes it falls on the fourth of Sivan, sometimes on the fifth, and sometimes on the sixth, that this is not the way of [other] festivals, which have a fixed date in the month that cannot be deviated from, neither earlier nor later. Since this is the case, the same should apply to Shavuot, that it should fall on a specific day, which is the sixth of Sivan. He sought proof for this in Jeremiah's words (Jeremiah 5:24) "He maintains for us the appointed weeks of the harvest." He said that the purpose of this is that Passover should not occur for Israel before the appointed times of harvest are found, which are the Omer from which until Shavuot. 2. And he said that the seven days are called Sabbath, [meaning] the entire week although it exists [as a separate term] and there are three workdays before and after it. And so these [days] are called the days of the Sabbath. And he said that the proof for this is in the Torah's words (Deuteronomy 16:9) "Seven weeks shall you count," etc., meaning from the time when the matter appears in the workdays, because they are called a week, as it says (Leviticus 12:5) "she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her menstruation," and for times of birth there is no fixed time. From this we learn that all seven days are called a week. Similarly, it says (Daniel 10:3) "till three whole weeks were fulfilled," and these were from the first of Nisan until the twenty-second of it, as is {861} clear from the context. And he said that the meaning of the verse (Leviticus 23:15) "seven Sabbaths" is seven weeks. He said: The exalted Creator did not command us to wave the Omer on a specific day [of the week], but rather the Sabbath is the only day of the week that He elevated. And he said that if this were the case [and there was a command for a specific day of the week] then this would constitute divination, as it would show preference for one day [of the week] over another, and this is not what God commanded the people of Israel. 3. He further said: Until our day, no one has understood the meaning of the verse (Leviticus 23:15) "from the morrow of the Sabbath," but the meaning is that the month [consists of] four Sabbaths, and from the beginning ... is called Sabbath. Therefore the Torah noted this in this verse, saying (ibid.) "and you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Sabbath," meaning the third Sabbath in Nisan (ibid. 16) "until the morrow of the seventh Sabbath.” 4. He further said: And so I will explain to you why He set the waving of the Omer for the morrow of Passover. This is because that is when the children of Israel left Egypt, as the firstborn died on the night of the fifteenth and remained thus for a night and day until they were buried on the sixteenth of Nisan. Therefore, the exalted God commanded that they offer from the first of the harvest on the day when Egypt's firstborn were cut down. And the Creator established a sign to remember this for generations, in the first of the land's harvest, in human firstborn and in animal firstborn, and He commanded the people of Israel to count [from] this time... new on the day... part of it. 5. As additional proof that the morrow of the Sabbath is the morrow of Passover, he brought the story of Joshua and said that the opinion of those who claim that this falls on Sunday [of the week], as we [the Karaites] interpret, is incorrect, since the scripture says (Joshua 1:10) "Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying: Pass through the midst of the camp [etc.] for within three days" etc. And it says (ibid. 2:23) "So the two men returned, and descended from the mountain." And it says (ibid. 3:1) "And Joshua rose early in the morning; and they removed from Shittim, etc. and they lodged there before they passed over and it came to pass at the end of three days, that the officers went through the midst of the camp; and they commanded the people, saying: When you see" etc., (ibid. 5) "And Joshua said unto the people: Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow" etc., (ibid. 4:19) "And the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth" etc. The four days mentioned here – the day of preparing provisions, the day... Shittim and day... the fourth day was on the tenth of Nisan, and Passover was on Monday night, which contradicts your words. And if the beginning of the four days was on Monday then Passover was on Tuesday night, and if their beginning was on Tuesday then Passover was on Wednesday night. Similarly, if their beginning was on Wednesday then Passover was on Thursday night, and if their beginning was on Thursday then Passover was {862} on Friday night, and if their beginning was on Friday then Passover was on Saturday night. And he said that in light of these reasons it is impossible to set four consecutive days for crossing [the Jordan], and therefore Passover certainly was not on Sunday night, as this would necessitate that the Sabbath was one of the four days of crossing.

content.hebrew: השער השביעי על אודות הטענות של המצדדים בחיבור [השמש והירח לקביעת המולד].
content.english: The Sixth Gate: Concerning the Refutation of Their Words

content.hebrew: 1. הם אמרו כי התורה אמרה (בראשית א:יד) 'והיו לאותות ולמועדים', וכן (תהלים קד:יט) 'עשה ירח למועדים שמש ידע מבואו', וכי דברו 'לאותות ולמועדים' מודיע כי שני המאורות יחד הם הסימנים והאותות למועדים, וכי אחד מהשניים אינו סימן למועדים [לבדו]. והשניים יכולים לסמן יחד [את תחילת החודש] רק אם הם מתחברים [ובאים בזמן אחד]. {799} וזה מורה על כך שחיבור השמש והירח הוא סימן לראש החודש שביום מסוים בתוכו חל המועד. וכך בדברו (תהלים קד:יט) 'עשה ירח למועדים' הכוונה היא כי זה קורה כאשר הירח והשמש נפגשים, שכן הוא אומר אחר כך 'שמש ידע מבואו'. כלומר לדעתם הוא מזדווג עם השמש בשקיעתה, שכן לשון 'ידע' מורה על זיווג, כדברו (בראשית ד:א) 'והאדם ידע את חוה אשתו', שפירושו הזדווג. וכן (שם יז) 'וידע קין את אשתו'. וכן הם הביאו לראיה את דברו (תהלים פא:ד) 'תקעו בחודש שופר', (שם ה) 'כי חק לישראל הוא', (שם ו) 'עדות ביהוסף שמו'. ואמרו כי דברו 'ביהוסף' מורה על זיווג השמש והירח. 2. והם מעלים שאלות שאין מטרתן לאשש את שיטתם בעניין החיבור והפירוד, אלא להקשות [על השיטה המצדדת] בראייה. [שאלות אלה] אינן שלהם בלבד, אלא גם אחרים כגון אנשי העיבור עשויים להקשות כך. אנו נזכיר אותן ונענה עליהן בפרק הבא.
content.english: 1. ... The opinion according to which the festival... within... what we mentioned before [from his words], that the festival follows the pattern of other appointed times and therefore falls on a specific day of the month, then the Torah would have specified this [day] and explained what it is just as it explained this for other appointed times, and it would not have deviated from what it did in all the others. [The fact that] it bounded [the appointed time] with two endpoints which are 'the morrow of the Sabbath' refutes his words. 2. Furthermore, if the Creator had already distinguished between the dates of the appointed times and set one at the beginning of the month, another on the tenth of the month, another on the fifteenth of the month, another on the twenty-first of the month and another on the twenty-second of the month, what would prevent Him from also setting [this festival]... in the month, and it may fall on the fourth, fifth and sixth of the month, since He set it as an end and limit to a count whose beginning is the beginning [of the offering time] of a sacrifice, which is also not fixed on a specific day of the month. This opinion is better and closer [to the truth] than its opposite, [that is] his opinion and his inclination from this to another. 3. As for Jeremiah's words that he cited (Jeremiah 5:24) "the appointed weeks of harvest" etc., who claimed otherwise? Indeed, this supports our view and not his, since we are the ones who determine the month of Aviv based on the ripening of barley and the readiness of seeds for harvest, while he determines it based on intercalation, which follows a fixed calculation. 4. As for his claim that the seven days are called 'Sabbath', meaning the entire week, regardless of whether the Sabbath falls at their beginning, middle, or end, he promised to present proof, [which turned out to] itself require additional proof. This refers to the Torah's words (Deuteronomy 16:9) "Seven weeks shall you count," [which according to him] is from the time it comes it begins, on one of the workdays. And if the meaning of these words is to require that the beginning of the harvest should be on the day of waving the Omer, and that this {863} must be a workday, it does not harm us whether this is on Sunday or another day. 5. And regarding the Torah's words that he cited (Leviticus 12:5) "she shall be unclean two weeks," and also (Daniel 10:3) "three whole weeks," the meaning is not [as he claims], for we have no doubt that any seven days are called a week, [regardless of] which day it begins and which day it ends. And already at the beginning of his words he promised that he [would succeed in] proving that the entire week is called 'Sabbath' [regardless of] whether the Sabbath falls at its beginning, or middle or end, but we do not see this and he has not shown demonstrative proof in this matter. 6. He also established that the Torah's words (Leviticus 23:15) "seven Sabbaths" is the explanation for "seven weeks." We too believe that these two verses refer to the same matter, but not because 'Sabbaths' are 'weeks', rather because the meaning of "weeks" is seven weeks and the meaning of "Sabbaths" is seven rest days, that is, seven Sabbath days. That is, the intention is that in the seven weeks there will be seven Sabbaths, meaning that the Sabbath day falls at the end of each week, not that the week is a Sabbath. Similarly, if the intention in the Torah's words (Leviticus 23:16) "until the morrow of the Sabbath" was to a week, this week would have to be entirely rest, since we do not find in the Torah 'Sabbath' that does not apply to rest, neither in relation to days nor in relation to years. One who claims otherwise must bring proof for this, and we have not found such proof. 7. And in this matter there is an issue where they oppose our words, and many of them do not understand it, but we must exhaust all their words to their end. [And their claim] is: that the Torah said (Leviticus 23:15) "seven complete Sabbaths shall there be," and if by "Sabbaths" the meaning is [to weeks] that the Sabbath [falls at their end] what then is the meaning of "complete"? Can seven such Sabbaths or fifteen or fewer or more not be complete? Therefore the meaning of "complete" must certainly refer to weeks and not to Sabbaths. The answer to this is [that "complete"] is a usage of the Hebrew language, similar to (Leviticus 25:29) "days shall be its redemption," where "days" means a year, and afterward it says (ibid. 30) "and if it is not redeemed until a complete year is fulfilled." If it had said "until a year is fulfilled" this would have been sufficient, since the completion of a year occurs only at the end of a [whole] year, [the addition of] "complete" is in the usage of language, as we said. 8. If their words were to decide for us then they would decide for them as well. This is because if we are talking about weeks, then it is known that a week is {864} [comprised of] seven days, [and a time of] less than seven days cannot be called a week. And if by saying (Leviticus 23:15) "seven Sabbaths" the meaning is seven weeks, what then is the meaning of "complete"? It is possible that the meaning of "complete" is that the days of the week will end and a complete week will end with the ending of the Sabbath. This is what was intended by “complete". 9. And someone might say: The Torah said (Leviticus 23:15) "And you shall count from the morrow of the Sabbath," and also (ibid.) "seven Sabbaths," and obligated us to count seven weeks from the morrow of the Sabbath. Therefore, if the meaning of "Sabbaths" were [complete weeks ending] on the Sabbath, and hence the morrow of the Sabbath was on Sunday, then we would be obligated to count the weeks from Sunday. However, it is not possible for Sunday to be part of the Sabbath. The answer to this is that "seven Sabbaths" (Leviticus 23:15) is not a conclusion to "and you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Sabbath," because after "and you shall count for yourselves" it explained what is meant, saying (Leviticus 23:16) "count fifty days." And "seven Sabbaths" is another matter that entered the discussion, and its meaning is that in these fifty days there will be seven [complete weeks ending] on the Sabbath. 10. And this is another question that one of them asked: The scripture says (Joshua 5:12) "And the manna ceased on the morrow," and this was on the fifteenth of Nisan. If this was on Sunday, it necessarily follows that on the fourteenth the manna fell, even though it was the Sabbath, and this contradicts the verse (Exodus 16:25) "today you shall not find it." And "the manna ceased on the morrow" parallels "and He rested on the seventh day" (Genesis 2:2), and just as "and He rested on the seventh day"... from the sixth, so... necessarily "morrow"... was... and this is why "on the morrow" is the sixteenth of Nisan according to their method, and that the manna fell on Passover on the fifteenth, which is a holy convocation, contradicting their words, since according to the Rabbanites the manna did not fall on festivals. 11. And in our opinion, it is possible that the meaning of the cessation of manna on the fifteenth is that it ceased falling at the time when it [usually] falls. And there was no need to mention the Sabbath and that it ceased falling on it, because this is its way and it never falls on any Sabbath. Rather, it mentioned only what it had to mention, namely that it ceased at a time when it usually does not cease and that at this time its matter ended. 12. And as for the proof that he sought in "and He rested on the seventh day" (Genesis 2:2), according to which this indicates that it happened on the sixth, the matter is not as he claims. This is because {865} he only... that it was on the seventh... but the performance of work... rather it became known through another proof, which is that the meaning of "and the manna ceased" (Joshua 5:12) is to indicate its cessation on the fifteenth only, and there is no proof in this that it was present on the fourteenth, and therefore the question is void. 13. And the one who asked this question argued that the meaning of "and the manna ceased on the morrow" (Joshua 5:12) refers to the day after the morrow, and in his opinion the morrow of Passover is the sixteenth, as we explained in his name. [According to this] "and the people ceased on the morrow" refers to the seventeenth, which is the morrow of the sixteenth. And this contradicts "when they ate of the produce of the land" (ibid.), since from here it necessarily follows that when they ate the new [crop] the manna ceased falling. And they [began] to eat the new [crop] on the thirteenth, and were not satisfied with postponing the morrow, which should be on the fifteenth, to the sixteenth but postponed it to the seventeenth. And this is similar to "and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished" (2 Chronicles 29:17). 14. Let us now return to what we were dealing with... the holder of the first opinion... rejoiced in this and announced... that no other person had understood this... today, and he does not know what is the meaning of "from the morrow of the Sabbath" (Leviticus 23:15), and that the meaning is that the month consists of four Sabbaths etc. And this is a rejected opinion, since in his previous words he relied on this [to prove] that seven [consecutive] days are called 'Sabbath'. And he had already said before... any time that falls... and this indicates without any doubt rest, and we do not find anything else in scripture at all. And it cannot be that the meaning of "until the morrow of the Sabbath" (ibid. 16) is until the morrow of the week, rather the meaning is the morrow of the seventh rest, which is the known and recognized Sabbath, namely Sunday. 15. And Jacob ben Ephraim al-Shami acknowledges that "until the morrow of the Sabbath" (Leviticus 23:16)... but from the morrow of the Sabbath... connection to the beginning... Sabbath... the fifteenth day... for he argued that the meaning of "until the morrow of the Sabbath" refers to rest, and the festival that is a holy convocation is the festival of Shavuot. And he said: the meaning of "until the morrow of the Sabbath" is "count fifty days from the sixteenth day which is the morrow of the Sabbath until the day of the festival of Shavuot," and the fiftieth day is included in the count and its morrow is {866} the fifty-first, and this is the meaning of "until the morrow of the Sabbath." And he said "count from the sixteenth day until the seventh of Sivan," which is fifty days from the morrow of the festival of Shavuot. And he did not include in this the morrow of the Sabbath in which he said "until the morrow of the Sabbath," because in his opinion when [the Torah] says "from one time until another time" it does not include in its words the other time. An example of this is the verse (Genesis 48:5) "until I came unto you in Egypt." This verse includes only those who were born before his arrival, while those who were born at the time of his arrival are not included in the matter. And so "until the morrow of the Sabbath" did not include the morrow in the matter. And he said that "the seventh" (Leviticus 23:16) does not refer to the Sabbath and does not mean there is a seventh festival, rather it refers to the morrow which is the day after the seven weeks, since each week has some morrow. 16. However, his argument has several flaws and defects. One is that in every place where the Torah says "until" the thing to which the "until" refers is included in the matter. An example of this is the verse (Exodus 13:15) "from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beast," and the beast is certainly included in the matter. And also "from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive" (ibid. 12:29). And there are many parallels that are known and therefore need not be mentioned. An even more prominent example is what is said regarding time, and regarding what is obligatory, the verse (ibid. 15) "for whosoever eats leavened bread, that soul shall be cut off" and also (ibid.) "from the first day until the seventh day," and the seventh about which "until" is said is included in the matter without doubt. And likewise "in the first month on the fourteenth day of the month at evening you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day" (ibid. 18) and the twenty-first day is included in its words. Whichever of these things would be better to compare to each other – days to days or obligation to obligation – in any case [it is interpreted] according to the customary way in scripture, and therefore in "until the morrow of the Sabbath" (Leviticus 23:16) the morrow of the Sabbath is included in the count of fifty, just as in "until the seventh day" the seventh is included in the prohibition of eating leavened bread. And so too in "until the twenty-first day" the twenty-first day is included in the obligation to eat unleavened bread. And likewise regarding the verse on which he relied (Genesis 48:5) "until I came unto you," in which he found no [proof at all]. 17. And on this matter ben Ephraim disagreed with all the Rabbanites [and in fact] with all Jews in the East and West. This is because there is no dispute that the second "morrow of the Sabbath" is included within {867} the fifty. [There are groups of] people who hold weak arguments until they do things that should not be done, and each one turns in [another] direction. And Daniel said that there was a group that claimed that the meaning of "until the morrow of the Sabbath" (Leviticus 23:16) is "you must count seven times, seven weeks, and afterward at the end of the seventh week cease counting, and on the morrow of the cessation of counting, on the fiftieth day, establish a festival." However, this opinion is weak, corrupt and impossible, because the cessation from counting is on the fiftieth day and not on the forty-ninth day, which is the last day of counting. [On this day] there is no cessation from counting but rather it is included in it, and the cessation is after it and following it. Therefore the fiftieth day is the day of cessation and its morrow is the fifty-first day. And according to their words the festival of Shavuot must be on the fifty-first day and this is impossible. And from every side it has been clarified that the beginning of counting the Omer is from Sunday [and its end] on Sunday, and this Sunday that comes following the Sabbath at the end of the seventh week is the festival of Shavuot. 18. And the holder of the first opinion said that he would explain why he set the waving of the Omer for the morrow of Passover, and then he brought arguments that have no proof or benefit whatsoever and there is no reason to engage with them. And as for the proof [he presumed to bring from the verse] (Joshua 1:10) "Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying" etc., this is quite simple, because he established four consecutive days without proof for this, when in fact it concerns three days. This is because it is not impossible that on the same day in which it is said "Joshua commanded the officers of the people [saying] pass through the midst of the camp" etc., the spies returned, as it says immediately afterward without interruption (ibid. 2:23) "So the two men returned, and descended from the mountain," from where does he know that their arrival was on another day? Rather, the day on which they came and on which provisions were prepared was Sunday, and they journeyed from Shittim on Monday and crossed the Jordan on Tuesday. And this day was the tenth of the month, and Sunday was the fifteenth of the month, and therefore his claim is refuted and our words are correct. 19. And someone might hold onto the verse (Joshua 1:11) "for within three days" [and claim] that from this verse it is required that the crossing was after three days, and if this was Sunday then the crossing must have been on Wednesday. However, this is not so, because "within" refers to the third day, similar to the verse (Genesis 40:13) "within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head" and it says there (ibid. 20) "and it came to pass on the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday."

content.hebrew: השער השמיני על אודות דחיית [דבריהם].
content.english: The Seventh Gate: Concerning That the Sunday on Which the Waving of the Omer Falls Is That Which Comes After the Offering of the Passover

content.hebrew: 1. יש להגיד להם: בטענתכם על אודות החיבור והפירוד אתם רומזים לדבר נסתר שאינו גלוי ואתם מציינים כי כדי להבין אותו יש צורך בחשבון דק ולא כל אדם יכול לעמוד על כך אלא רק יחידי סגולה ורק מי שיגע ודרש עד שהשיג ועמד על כך. אולם האם יש מצווה כלשהי שהאל יתעלה חייב את האומה כולה לעשותה ושהיא נסתרת מחושיהם ומראייתם, או מצווה שהאל חייב אותם לעשותה אך לא פירשה וציינה בתורתו? ואם האל יתעלה חייב אותנו בחיבור ופירוד וזה דבר שדורש חשבון דק כדי להבינו, כלום לא יבאר בתורתו את החשבון הזה וילמד לאנשים את דרכו וטעמיו ואופניו? ומדוע הוא לא עשה זאת כך שאם הם ירצו לדעת זאת ולעמוד על כך [יוכלו] ללכת בדרך שהוא לימד אותם ולא יבואו לידי טעות? בנוסף לכך, הכרת החיבור והפירוד היא חלק ממדע הכוכבים [=אסטרונומיה] וחשבונם, ואם כן האם ייתכן שהאל יחייב {800} את האדם במועדים ובראשי החודשים ויפנה אותם אל האסטרונומים כדי שילמדו [את התאריכים הנכונים] מהם? דעה זו אינה אלא עקשנות באשר לתבונה ולחיוב המצוות יחדיו, וכן הדבר באשר לאנשי העיבור. 2. הם עשויים לענות על כך ולהגיד: האל ישתבח חייב [אותנו] בצרעת אך מסר את הכרת [הצרעת] והבנת מהותה לקבוצה מסוימת בלבד, שהם הכוהנים. ומאחר שכך הדבר אין לשלול כי הוא יחייב במועדים ובראשי חודשים וימסור את הכרתם לקבוצה מסוימת, שאליה יש לפנות ועל פיה יש לפסוק. [על כך] יש להגיד להם: כאשר הבורא יתעלה ייחד את עניין הצרעת לקבוצה מסוימת הוא לא הפקיר אותנו כך שלא נדע מי היא הקבוצה הזו, אלא יידע אותנו ואמר לנו מי הם במקומות רבים. אילו היה הדבר כך באשר להכרת המועדים וראשי החודשים הוא היה מיידע אותנו ואומר לנו מי היא הקבוצה הזו שיש לפסוק על פיה. ומאחר שהוא לא עשה זאת דעה זו היא בטלה, וטענתכם אינה כפי שאתם סוברים שהיא, שכן שופט אינו יכול לחייב דבר מה ואז להסתיר מהאנשים דבר מה ולא לבאר זאת ולא להודיע לנו מי הם האנשים שיש לפסוק על פיהם. [הראיה] שהבאתם לדבריכם היא ראיה נגדכם ולא לטובתכם. 3. ואם הם ישובו ויתנגדו לדברינו על ידי היקש, באופן דומה למה שאנו עשינו במולד ובעיבור, [ויגידו]: אילו היה האל מחייב אותנו בזה הוא היה מיידע אותנו באופני הדבר ובדרכיו. אם כן, היאך עלינו לקיים זאת כאשר האופנים הדרכים הללו מרובים וכל קבוצה נוקטת בשיטה משלה? אנו נגיד: השימוש בהיקש הוא דבר שהשכל מחייב והוא נמצא בנפש, והצורך להשתמש בו הוא הכרחי. וכבר ביארנו זאת במאמר השני בספר זה. ואין זה דרך הפירוד והעיבור, שאין הוכחה לאף אחד מהם. 4. עוד יש להגיד להם: כאשר התורה הפנתה את עניין הצרעת אל הכוהנים וייחסה לקביעתם את ההיטמאות היא לא הניחה לזה אלא ביארה ופירשה את זה בבירור תכליתי ורמזה לזה באופן שהחוש יכול להשיג ולהבין, [באמצעות דברים כמו ציון] הצבעים, השקעים, ההתפשטות והפשֹייה, הנפיחוּת, העמידה [וסימנים] נוספים שכל האנשים יכולים להשיג ולחוש ולהבין. היא לא רמזה בזה לדבר נסתר, שצריך להסיק באופן אזוטרי וחבוי. [באופן זה], אם הכוהן טועה [בשיפוטו] כך שהוא סותר את הדבר ופוסק [על טהור] שהוא טמא, וכן ההפך, האנשים יכולים להשיב לו ולהעמיד אותו על טעותו. אילו היו דבריכם על אודות החיבור והפירוד או העיבור נכונים [האל] היה מיידע זאת ומבאר זאת בתורתו ומלמד את האנשים כפי שהוא ביאר להם {801} ולימד אותם את סימני הצרעת ותנאיה. ובזה שהוא נמנע מכך יש [כדי ללמד] על השקר שלהם. 5. ובהתנגדותם לראייה הם עשויים להגיד: אם אכן האל יתעלה חייב [אותנו] בראייה, למה אפוא הוא לא ביאר זאת ולימד אותנו? יש להגיד להם: בעניין הראייה אין דבר שמצריך הסבר, הוראה וביאור, שכן הגדול והקטן, החכם והבור, [כולם] מבינים זאת. וזה בניגוד למה שאתם אומרים בעניין החיבור והפירוד והעיבור, שרק מעטים ומתי מעט מבינים זאת וזה מצריך היסק וחישוב דק. ודבר כגון זה קורא בהכרח לצורך בביאור, בהוראה ובלימוד הטובים ביותר. 6. ואם הם יגידו: מדוע הוא לא אמר אם כן 'בראותכם את הירח קִבעו את ראש החודש'?
